image_description: A side-profile view of a large American Bison standing on a dirt path. The bison has a massive, shaggy dark brown forequarter with a prominent shoulder hump and a beard. The hindquarters are less furry and smoother. It has short curved horns, small ears hidden in fur, and sturdy legs ending in hooves. A short tail with a bushy tuft is visible. In the background, other bison are grazing in a green field.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile, showing a broad structure and short, upward-curving horns consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, shaggy beard hangs from the chin and throat area, matching the taxonomy description.
The eye is visible as a dark spot on the side of the head, consistent with the description.
Ears are not prominently sticking out; they appear small and nestled within the thick fur of the head/neck region.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits the characteristic heavy build and high shoulder hump typical of bison.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The forequarters are covered in thick, dark, shaggy fur that creates a very distinct shoulder hump.
There is a clear visual transition from the shaggy front to the smoother, shorter-haired hindquarters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horns are visibly short relative to the massive size of the head and body.

The legs appear sturdy and proportionate. While the ground obscures the exact hoof detail, the lower leg structure is consistent with cloven-hoofed animals, and no anomalies like extra legs or melting are visible.
The tail is visible hanging down, ending in a distinct dark bushy tuft.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out hybrid or generic bovid errors.
To verify the structural integrity of the four legs and spine alignment, ensuring no limb fusion or missing parts.
To check for edge bleeding between the shaggy fur and the background, and ensure the tail and beard are topologically connected.
To assess overall texture consistency of the fur and detect any subtle generation artifacts or blurring.

focus_areas: Fur texture consistency (shaggy vs smooth transition)
Boundary sharpness around the beard and tail
Anatomical correctness of the shoulder hump
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition zone between the shaggy forequarters and the smoother hindquarters. AI often struggles with this textural boundary. Also, verify that the legs do not merge into the belly fur or the ground. Check if the horn curvature is physically plausible for a bison.
